claims.text: EF Core docs: calling LINQ operators just builds an in-memory representation of the query; the query is only sent to the database when results are consumed (a for/foreach loop, or ToList/ToArray/Single/Count and their async overloads). The DbContext (DonHangDbContext) is what sends that SQL.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/querying/how-query-works.md, "When queries are executed"

claims.text: EF Core docs: the provider translates the database-evaluable parts of a LINQ query to SQL, sent once. FirstOrDefaultAsync(predicate) puts the predicate in that SQL and returns the first match, or null if none.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/querying/how-query-works.md, "The life of a query"; EntityFrameworkQueryableExtensions.FirstOrDefaultAsync API

claims.text: EF Core docs: by default (single query mode), Include loads related entities via JOINs in one query; Đơn Hàng stage-1 sets no split mode. A collection JOIN returns one row per item, order columns repeated; EF builds one Order holding all Items.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, querying/single-split-queries.md (+ "Data duplication"), querying/tracking.md "Identity resolution"; examples/don-hang @ stage-1 (no SplitQuery in *.cs)
